methods.summary: The access requests waiting for the owner.

methods.name: cards.list
methods.summary: The cards waiting (oldest first) and the owner's recent closed ones (newest first), as `{open, recent}`.

methods.name: cards.show
methods.summary: One card in full, with its options and who holds its claim. Refuses an id that is no card.

params.name: id
params.summary: The card.

methods.name: cards.answer
methods.summary: Answers a card. Answers `{result: answered}` (with the card's new state), `closed` (it was already answered, withdrawn or expired), `expired` (its time ran out first) or `claimed` (another answerer holds it). Refuses a secret card (a key or access ask: answer it in the Kith app), an unknown card and an answer the card does not offer.

params.name: id
params.summary: The card.

params.name: answer
params.summary: The answer: one of the card's option ids, or allow, deny or cancel when it lists none.

methods.name: cards.provide
methods.summary: Types a key into a key card: the core claims the card, seals every value into the secrets envelope and spends the card in one commit, at most once. Answers `{result: saved}` (names only: the service, account and variables, never a value), `closed` (answered, denied, saved or withdrawn already), `expired` (its time ran out first) or `claimed` (another provide holds it). A failed write changes nothing and leaves the card open. Refuses a card that is not a key card, an account name that is taken or unusable, and values that do not match the card. The values are never logged or echoed; a terminal does not type them, an app fills them in.

params.name: id
params.summary: The key card.

params.name: account
params.summary: The account name for a new key (the card names it when it replaces one).

params.name: values
params.summary: The key's fields by variable name. Never written on a command line.

methods.name: secrets.open
methods.summary: Load the machine's secrets key from the OS key store (making it on a first use), so later calls do not wait for the store.

methods.name: secrets.has
methods.summary: Whether a secret of that name is stored. Needs no key, so it never waits on the OS key store.

params.name: name
params.summary: The secret's name.

methods.name: secrets.delete
methods.summary: Remove a secret. Needs no key.

params.name: name
params.summary: The secret's name.

methods.name: secrets.get
methods.summary: A secret's value, or that there is none.

params.name: name
params.summary: The secret's name.

methods.name: secrets.put
methods.summary: Store a secret sealed under the machine's key, replacing an earlier value of that name.

params.name: name
params.summary: The secret's name.

params.name: value
params.summary: The value, from the caller (never a word of the command line).

methods.name: gate.list
methods.summary: The gate's slots and the line, in the order the line is kept. Frees holders whose process is gone first.

methods.name: gate.take
methods.summary: Asks for a slot. Answers `granted`, `waiting` (with a position), `parked` (gave its slot up, not in line) or `gone` (holds nothing). Asking again for the same holder changes nothing.

params.name: holder
params.summary: The run or claim that wants the slot.

params.name: rt
params.summary: The actor it belongs to (display only; the holder when absent).

params.name: max
params.summary: How many slots there are (1 or more). Remembered; later takes may leave it out.

params.name: invitee
params.summary: An invited person's turn: behind the owner's, and few at once.

params.name: pid
params.summary: The holder's process (2 or more), so a crash frees the slot.

methods.name: gate.release
methods.summary: Gives a slot or a place in line back. Releasing a holder that holds nothing does nothing.

params.name: holder
params.summary: The run or claim.

methods.name: gate.park
methods.summary: The holder waits on another bot's reply: its slot is given up. Nested asks share one parking.

params.name: holder
params.summary: The run or claim.

methods.name: gate.unpark
methods.summary: One ask is back; the last one puts the holder in line again, ahead of turns that have not started.

params.name: holder
params.summary: The run or claim.

methods.name: syncLease.status
methods.summary: Whether this Mac is in sync with the cloud. Answers `cloud` (`unknown`, `linked` or `off`), `synced`, `held` (what a non-owner's claim needs: the cloud is off, or linked with the lease unexpired), `until` (ms) and `mark`.

methods.name: syncLease.link
methods.summary: The cloud is on: the lease decides from now on, and it is not held until a pull says so. Linking again changes nothing.

methods.name: syncLease.unlink
methods.summary: The cloud is off on purpose: nothing waits on it, and any lease is gone.

methods.name: syncLease.mark
methods.summary: Where the cloud's changes stand. Take it before a pull reads the cloud's state, and give it back to `syncLease.pulled`.

methods.name: syncLease.changed
methods.summary: The cloud said its state changed: the lease ends at once, until a pull that started after this succeeds. Answers the new `mark`.

methods.name: syncLease.drop
methods.summary: The connection to the cloud dropped or is being made: the lease ends. Dropping when nothing is held does nothing.

methods.name: syncLease.pulled
methods.summary: A pull of the cloud's state succeeded. Answers `held: true` when the lease now runs, `held: false` when it does not: the cloud changed since the mark, the cloud is not linked, or the clock is behind its last reading.

params.name: mark
params.summary: The `mark` taken before the pull read the cloud's state.

params.name: ms
params.summary: How long the lease runs, 1 to 3600000 (120000 when absent).

methods.name: syncLease.renew
methods.summary: The relay was heard: runs a held lease out again. Answers `renewed: true`, or `renewed: false` when nothing is held to renew (never acquired, lost, expired or the clock is behind): only a pull acquires.

params.name: ms
params.summary: How long the lease runs from now, 1 to 3600000 (120000 when absent).

methods.name: doors.list
methods.summary: The guest doors that are starting or live, and swept ones whose box is not confirmed gone, as `{doors}`. With `--all` the closed ones kept for a day too.

params.name: all
params.summary: Include doors that ended or were confirmed gone.

methods.name: doors.start
methods.summary: Starts a door for a person: the access check and the row in one step. Answers the door (`state` starting, its `version`) and `repeat` (true when this id was already starting or live, nothing written). Refuses, as `kith-auth door` does: the owner (doors are for the people an agent is shared with), a person who is cut off or may not run the agent, a Mac out of sync with the cloud, a door that is not among the doors their ticked jobs grant now (a bot's cut to its owner's); then a supervisor that is not running and an id that is a swept or ended door.

params.name: agent
params.summary: The agent whose door it is.

params.name: door
params.summary: The door as `name@digest`, the piece a job grants.

params.name: person
params.summary: The person (or bot) it runs for.

params.name: folder
params.summary: The person's folder it runs on (display only).

params.name: id
params.summary: The door's id, 16 hex digits (a new one when absent). A start retried with it is the same door.

params.name: pid
params.summary: The supervisor's process (2 or more), so a crash is found by its start time.

params.name: kernel
params.summary: The kernel folder (default: the one this program finds).

params.name: home
params.summary: The caller's home folder (a daemon has its own).

params.name: env
params.summary: The caller's KITH_* and HQ_* variables (a daemon has its own).

methods.name: doors.markLive
methods.summary: The supervisor says the box is up. Answers `{result: live}`, or `{result: lost, state}` when a sweep (or an end) got to the door first: the box must not run. Only a `starting` door at this `version` goes live.

params.name: id
params.summary: The door.

params.name: version
params.summary: The version `doors.start` answered.

methods.name: doors.end
methods.summary: The box is gone. An open door becomes ended; a swept one is confirmed gone (it stays swept). Answers `{result: ended}` or `{result: swept}`. Ending twice changes nothing; refuses an id that is no door.

params.name: id
params.summary: The door.

methods.name: doors.sweep
methods.summary: Marks swept every open door of the named people and their bots, every door whose supervisor is gone, and (unless `--no-recheck`) every door whose person may no longer run its agent. Answers `swept` (this call's) and `pending` (swept before, box not confirmed gone). The owner is never swept by a name, only for a gone supervisor. Kills nothing.

params.name: persons
params.summary: People whose doors all end.

params.name: noRecheck
params.summary: Do not ask again whether each person may still run their door (it does by default).

params.summary: The kernel folder (default: the one this program finds).

params.name: home
params.summary: The caller's home folder (a daemon has its own).

params.name: env
params.summary: The caller's KITH_* and HQ_* variables (a daemon has its own).

Harness.description: The program an agent runs on: `harness:` in its agent.md (`claude-code` is printed as claude), or a backup entry's. The host starts claude, codex, and any engine of the core's table with an ACP mode (`kith engines`); `agy` is the kernel's word for antigravity. One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host doesn't start it.

RolePrompt.description: How an engine takes the agent's role prompt, from the engine table's `enforces`: `flag` (a flag or ACP option on the command line), `env` (an environment variable), `first-message` (in front of the first message), `none` (not known to be deliverable: the host puts it in front of the first message). One this version doesn't know is read as none.

PermissionMode.description: The Claude Code permission mode a run starts in (kernel/lib/kith_settings.py CHOICES); a Codex run gets the host's translation. One this version doesn't know starts the run in default, which asks before every change.

DelegationState.description: Where a delegation (one `kith ask` id) stands: `open` (running, or parked on a card), `answered`, `capped` (answered, and its run took the chain to its cost cap) or `stopped` (the run gave no answer). One this version doesn't know is its own state: the host leaves it alone.

Agent.description: One agent in `kith ls --json`. `home` is its folder, where its bot works. A kernel from before `harness` was listed runs every agent on Claude. `builtin` is true for an agent that ships with kith (like scratch): never backed up or shared; older kernels leave it out.

NewAgent.description: `kith new <name> <description> --json`: the agent just made. `home` is its folder (memory, data and files beside the role), `dir` its role folder (its own repo: agent.md, settings.json, skills). A failure prints `{"ok": false, "error": "..."}` and exits non-zero instead, and leaves no folder behind.

Projects.description: `kith project ls --json`: every registered project, sorted by id.

Project.description: One registered project: its paths (absolute), its home folder when it has one, its git remotes, the project it sits in, its shared memory folder, and whether a folder of it is on this Mac.

Launch.description: `kith <agent> --launch-json`: how to start the agent, for claude and codex and, additively, any other engine the table lists with an ACP mode: `engine` is the table id (left out for claude and codex, which print what they always did), `acp` the installed CLI's own ACP program (null when it has none here: the host then starts the `registry` build), `role_prompt` how the engine takes `system_prompt`. `settings` is Claude Code's settings (null for another harness), `mcp_servers` its servers in Claude's format, `claude_args` the arguments `kith <agent>` would give claude (null for another harness). `backup`, `provider` and `account` say which backup entry, harness and login answer the run; `account_id` is that login as a backup id (`claude`, `claude:work`, `codex`), the agent's main account or the `--backup` entry.

AcpStart.description: How to start an engine over ACP, from the engine table (`kith kernel engines launch <id> --json`): the installed CLI's own ACP mode as a program. `env` is extra environment for it (the engine's keys are the host's own).

CostTag.description: What the cost ledger files a run's usage under. `via` is where the run came from (terminal, serve, a channel).

Delegations.description: `kith ask delegations --json`: every delegation record on this Mac, newest first.

Delegation.description: The record of one `kith ask` id (foreground, --bg or agent@machine), in kernel/bin/kith-ask's ~/.kith/live/ask/ID.reg. `agent` is the agent asked, `chain` the id of the root ask of its chain, `hop` its depth (0 at the root) and `cross_hops` how many asks of the chain crossed to another Mac. Money is in micro-dollars (US$1 = 1000000) at API prices; `cost_micro_usd` is null for an ask from before costs were kept. `cap_micro_usd` is the chain cap in force now (null: none). `capped_ms` is when this ask's run took its chain to that cap, and `cap_card_ms` when the host raised the Needs-you card for it (once per chain and cap). Times are ms. A record from before delegation records reads as a root ask: chain = its id, hop 0. `brief` is the ask's text (at most 2000 characters) and `session` the asked agent's session once a --bg run claimed one; both are for the owner's peek, null on an older record, and never part of a member's or bot's RPC.

Caller.description: Who asked: the agent (null for a terminal), the person whose run it is (null for the owner) and where it came from (`terminal`, `serve`, ...).

ReplyTo.description: Where the answer goes: the caller's session (a wake once nobody waits for it) and the ask whose run asked. This is the only place the address lives; cards never carry it.

KernelVersion.description: `kith kernel version`: the interface version and the modules this build answers.

Engines.description: `kith kernel engines --json`: the coding engines, installed or not, as the engine table describes them.

LaunchPrompt.description: `kith kernel launch prompt --json`: the system prompt a run gets.
